summary:
The main purpose of the National Road Safety Act, 2083 is to make legal provisions regarding road safety management and promotion to develop and implement safety standards for road infrastructure construction for safe roads, to reduce human and economic losses from road accidents, and to prevent and minimize road accidents (Preamble, Page 1). This Act comes into force on the thirty-first day from the date of authentication (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

Federal, provincial, and local level road bodies carry out road design, construction, and maintenance (Section 2, Clause (ja), Page 1). To promote road safety at the provincial level, a Province Road Safety Coordination Committee is formed under the chairmanship of the Minister looking after provincial road infrastructure, with secretaries of provincial ministries, representatives of security bodies, and subject experts, up to a maximum of 11 members (Section 16, Subsection 1, Page 8). The functions, duties, and powers of this committee include coordinating with the Council on road safety, conducting provincial-level road safety programs, raising awareness, implementing and causing the implementation of Council recommendations, sending an annual report of road safety activities to the Council, and doing other work specified by provincial law (Section 16, Subsection 2, Page 8). To promote road safety at the local level, a Local Road Safety Coordination Committee is formed under the convenorship of an executive member designated by the head or chairperson of the local level (Section 17, Subsection 1, Page 8). The functions, duties, and powers of this committee include coordinating with the Province Committee and Council, running programs and awareness campaigns in coordination with the Council, implementing and causing the implementation of recommendations, preparing and sending an annual report to the Council, and performing other necessary work (Section 17, Subsection 2, Page 8-9).

Road-related agencies must recommend route permits to transport bodies based on suitability and types of vehicles after road construction is completed and inform the Council (Section 9, Page 6). Road-related agencies must repair dilapidated or damaged roads in accident-prone areas as soon as possible and carry out improvement work based on road safety audits (Section 10, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 6). During repairs, reconstruction, or upgrading, or when movement is stopped due to accidents, road-related agencies must keep transport services running by placing standard traffic signs or constructing temporary roads where technically feasible (Section 11, Page 6). Road-related agencies shall direct relevant bodies to manage other physical structures within road boundaries, such as trees, electric poles, communications, water supply, or drainage (Section 13, Subsection 1, Page 6-7). Road-related agencies must prepare national road safety action plans with estimated costs, prepare land-use plans, manage budgets, use modern technologies, construct and maintain roads according to standards, and conduct road safety audits (Section 18, Clauses (a) to (g), Page 9). Road-related agencies must determine maximum speed limits for vehicles on roads and display or install notices or signs at appropriate intervals (Section 22, Subsections 1 and 2, Page 11). Road-related agencies must formulate and implement road safety codes of conduct, and drivers, operators, employees, and road users must comply with such codes of conduct (Section 26, Subsections 1 and 3, Page 13). Transport bodies must issue route permits after registration only upon ensuring compliance with laws regarding public transport standards and safety (Section 21, Page 11). Transport bodies must enforce separate standards for professional driver's licenses for public transport drivers (Section 24, Subsection 2, Page 12). Health institutions to which injured victims are brought have a duty to treat them (Section 29, Subsection 1, Page 14) and must digitally update records of injured persons undergoing treatment or dying during treatment (Section 29, Subsection 4, Page 14). The Council must submit an annual report to the Nepal Government within 3 months from the date of completion of each fiscal year (Section 44, Subsection 1, Page 19).

The Council may conduct training to develop technical manpower for road safety auditors (Section 14, Subsection 1, Page 7). Individuals with prescribed qualifications participating in the training and passing the test shall be granted a road safety auditor certificate by the Council (Section 14, Subsections 2 and 3, Page 7). The Council may cancel the certificate at any time if testing is not conducted according to standards or if a false report is submitted (Section 14, Subsection 5, Page 7). The Council may issue directives to transport bodies regarding teaching materials, examination syllabus, health tests during renewal, and maintaining examination standards when issuing driver's licenses (Section 24, Subsection 1, Page 12). The Council issues minimum safety standards for road construction, road safety audit standards, quality standards for structure construction materials and construction processes, standards for manufacturing and importing vehicle safety equipment, and quality standards for road maintenance (Section 8, Clause (b), Page 4-5).

The bill creates the National Road Safety Council (Section 3, Subsection 1, Page 2). The main functions, duties, and powers of the Council are to approve operating policies, plans, annual budget, and programs; issue road safety standards and quality specifications; coordinate with government and non-government bodies; monitor and evaluate compliance with standards and audits; conduct research; establish central information management systems; and provide advice, suggestions, and recommendations to the Nepal Government (Section 8, Clauses (a) to (g), Page 4-6).
